The cumulative baseline hazard of a given shape

Source: R/derive-tdt-ttl.R
H0_of.Rd

Returns the function H0(tau) for the chosen baseline. Under the memoryless shape it is elapsed exposure itself; the Weibull, log-logistic and Gompertz shapes let the hazard rise or fall with how long the individual has already been exposed. Shape and scale arrive as per-draw vectors, and elapsed time may be a vector or a matrix whose rows are draws.

Usage

H0_of(baseline)

Arguments

baseline

A character string, a key of h0_catalogue: "mem", "weibull", "llogis" or "gompertz".

Value

A function of (tau, shape, scale) giving the cumulative baseline hazard. What shape and scale mean depends on the baseline:

  • "mem": both are ignored.

  • "weibull" and "llogis": shape is k and scale is s.

  • "gompertz": shape is the rate constant gamma and scale is ignored.

Details

For the Gompertz shape the first argument is the rate constant gamma and the second is ignored. A negative gamma is a valid value and means a hazard that falls the longer the individual has been exposed. The cumulative hazard then levels off: it rises towards 1/|gamma| but never reaches it, instead of growing without limit. Survival therefore never drops to zero, and the model predicts that some individuals never fail (a cure fraction, in survival-analysis terms). H0inv_of() gives the time by which a chosen fraction of individuals has failed; when that fraction is never reached it returns NaN for the time, rather than a large number standing in for "never".

Examples

# The memoryless baseline is elapsed exposure itself.
H0_of("mem")(tau = c(10, 30, 60), shape = 1, scale = 1)
#> [1] 10 30 60

# A Weibull baseline with shape 2 and scale 60: H0(tau) = (tau / 60)^2.
H0_of("weibull")(tau = 30, shape = 2, scale = 60)
#> [1] 0.25
